display.purpose: Copperplate engraved caps — artist name, section plates, category labels. Always uppercase, tracked.

body.purpose: Cormorant weight 300 — bios, project descriptions, statements. Held at ~60ch.

label.purpose: futura-pt geometric caps — descriptors, scroll cue, micro-labels. Tracking ≥0.30em.

shadows.name: glow-bone
shadows.purpose: Emergent light on dark-world controls (arrow buttons) on hover/focus. Soft, non-directional porcelain bloom — not elevation.

shadows.name: penumbra-ink
shadows.purpose: Emergent light on light-world controls (pills, light-theme arrows). Soft ink penumbra as objects settle under glass.

shadows.name: bone-halo
shadows.purpose: Faint porcelain ring around the active pill lozenge, paired with penumbra-ink.

motion.name: ease-signature
motion.purpose: The single system easing (ease-out-quart family). Every transition and entrance uses it.

motion.name: pill-spring
motion.purpose: The active-pill fill sliding between category tabs (layoutId).

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Control invert-on-hover (200ms) and nav link/color-theme flips (300ms).

motion.name: section-dissolve
motion.purpose: Adjacent full-viewport sections crossfade through the graphite ground. Opacity only.

components.name: Category Pill (active)
components.description: The selected Work category tab — a dark lozenge floating on a soft ink penumbra with a faint flesh halo; slides between tabs.
components.css: .ds-pill-active { position: relative; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 8px 22px; background: var(--oxidized-graphite, #1A1A1C); color: var(--bone-porcelain, #F3EEE8); font-family: 'futura-pt', 'Copperplate Gothic Light', sans-serif; font-size: 9.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.20em; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 8px 22px -12px rgba(26,26,28,0.65), 0 0 0 4px rgba(201,164,143,0.05); }

components.name: Category Pill (inactive)
components.description: An unselected Work category — a quiet blurred form that warms with a taupe glow and lifts on attention. Settling under glass, not a dashed placeholder.
components.css: .ds-pill-inactive { position: relative; border: 1px solid rgba(26,26,28,0.10); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 8px 22px; background: rgba(143,120,108,0.05); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(3px); backdrop-filter: blur(3px); color: rgba(26,26,28,0.85); font-family: 'futura-pt', 'Copperplate Gothic Light', sans-serif; font-size: 9.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.20em; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), border-color 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), box-shadow 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), transform 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-pill-inactive:hover, .ds-pill-inactive:focus-visible { border-color: rgba(143,120,108,0.40); background: rgba(143,120,108,0.09); box-shadow: 0 8px 22px -12px rgba(26,26,28,0.65); transform: translateY(-1px); }

components.name: Arrow Button (light theme)
components.description: Square gallery/next-project control on a light surface. Emergent light — surfaces with an ink penumbra on hover, no invert.
components.html: <button class="ds-arrow-light" aria-label="Next image"><svg width="13" height="13" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><path d="M9 6l6 6-6 6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-arrow-light { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 36px; height: 36px; border: 1px solid rgba(26,26,28,0.10); border-radius: 0; background: rgba(26,26,28,0.02); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(3px); backdrop-filter: blur(3px); color: rgba(26,26,28,0.70); cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), background-color 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), border-color 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), box-shadow 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), transform 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-arrow-light:hover, .ds-arrow-light:focus-visible { color: var(--oxidized-graphite, #1A1A1C); border-color: rgba(143,120,108,0.40); background: rgba(143,120,108,0.08); box-shadow: 0 8px 22px -12px rgba(26,26,28,0.65); transform: translateY(-1px) scale(1.03); } .ds-arrow-light:active { transform: scale(0.94); }

components.name: Arrow Button (dark theme)
components.description: Same control on a dark surface — a faint form that emerges from shadow with a soft porcelain bloom on hover, no invert.
components.html: <button class="ds-arrow-dark" aria-label="Next image"><svg width="13" height="13" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><path d="M9 6l6 6-6 6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-arrow-dark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 36px; height: 36px; border: 1px solid rgba(243,238,232,0.10); border-radius: 0; background: rgba(243,238,232,0.03); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(3px); backdrop-filter: blur(3px); color: rgba(243,238,232,0.70); cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), background-color 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), border-color 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), box-shadow 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), transform 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-arrow-dark:hover, .ds-arrow-dark:focus-visible { color: var(--bone-porcelain, #F3EEE8); border-color: rgba(201,164,143,0.40); background: rgba(201,164,143,0.07); box-shadow: 0 0 26px -6px rgba(201,164,143,0.55), inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(201,164,143,0.22); transform: translateY(-1px) scale(1.03); } .ds-arrow-dark:active { transform: scale(0.94); }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Floating Copperplate nav link — rests dimmed, rises to full on hover and catches a soft flesh underglow behind the label. Color auto-flips per section.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { position: relative; font-family: 'Copperplate Gothic Light', 'Copperplate', Georgia, serif; font-size: 14px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.20em; color: rgba(243,238,232,0.55); text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-nav-link::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; width: 130%; height: 210%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); background: radial-gradient(closest-side, rgba(201,164,143,0.42), transparent 75%); filter: blur(6px); opacity: 0; z-index: -1; pointer-events: none; transition: opacity 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { color: var(--bone-porcelain, #F3EEE8); } .ds-nav-link:hover::after, .ds-nav-link:focus-visible::after { opacity: 0.55; }

narrative.overview: The site is a clinical display case for a practice about the body under engineering. Work is presented as specimens — lit from the dark, held still, examined — and the interface is the vitrine: cold, exact glass that frames a charged, bodily subject without ever competing with it. The whole experience runs two registers of the same case: a dark world (the lit vitrine — oxidized-graphite ground, cinematic imagery, hairline serifs) carries atmosphere and first impression, and a light world (the catalogue card — bone-porcelain ground, dark ink, taxonomic labels) carries the index. The single fixed nav flips between them automatically, so moving through the site feels like turning a specimen from its dramatic display into its documentation and back. Density is low and deliberate; depth is soft and atmospheric, not stacked — no drop shadows, only tonal gradients, opacity dissolves, and functional text-shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Two-world system: dark cinematic vitrine ↔ light catalogue index, nav auto-flips.
Specimen-first: imagery leads, the interface recedes to glass.
Atmospheric depth, zero drop shadows — dissolves, gradients, crossfades.
Hairline, uppercase, widely-tracked typography as instrument labeling.
Refined unease by precision and low light, never by shock.

rules.name: The Two-Worlds Rule
rules.body: Every surface is either dark-world (oxidized-graphite ground, bone-porcelain type, data-nav-theme dark) or light-world (bone-porcelain ground, oxidized-graphite type, data-nav-theme light). There is no third ground; new sections declare their world and never invent a mid-gray in between.

rules.name: The One-Skin Rule
rules.body: synthetic-flesh is the only accent and it is rare — reserved for moments that reference the body (accents, hovers, the descriptor). It is prohibited as a button fill, a background, or a section device. Its scarcity is what makes it read as flesh and not as brand color.

rules.name: The Tracked-Caps Rule
rules.body: Every Copperplate and Futura label is uppercase and widely tracked (≥0.20em). Sentence-case display type is forbidden; these fonts are labels, not headlines.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Cormorant body always runs at weight 300, never bolder. The thin literary line is the reading voice of the whole system; a heavier body weight reads as a different, wrong site.

rules.name: The Emergent-Light Rule
rules.body: Structural drop shadows are prohibited — no directional offset simulating a lifted panel. Shadow is permitted only as emergent light on controls: soft, diffuse, porcelain- or ink-toned, tied to state, tokenized as --glow-bone / --penumbra-ink. A hard offset drop shadow anywhere is still a bug.

rules.name: The Glass-Is-For-Controls Rule
rules.body: backdrop-filter: blur() is allowed only as a ≤3px functional lift of an interactive control off imagery. Frosted panels, glass cards, and decorative blur on surfaces remain prohibited.

rules.name: The Functional-Glow Rule
rules.body: text-shadow exists to keep light type readable over dark imagery, and the nav-link underglow (--glow-underlay) to raise a link on hover. Neither is applied to static type on a solid surface for effect.

dos: Do anchor every surface to one of the two worlds (dark #1A1A1C ground / #F3EEE8 type, or light #F3EEE8 ground / #1A1A1C type) and declare its data-nav-theme.
Do let imagery lead — the specimen holds the room; type, spacing, and motion frame it.
Do keep all display/label type uppercase and tracked ≥0.20em (Copperplate) and body type Cormorant weight 300.

Do convey depth with tonal gradients, opacity dissolves, and the wet-petroleum step — atmospheric, not stacked. Controls are the one place light gathers: a soft emergent glow on hover/focus (--glow-bone dark, --penumbra-ink light).

Do reserve synthetic-flesh (#C9A48F) for rare, body-referencing text accents and hovers only — never for a rule, tick, border or ring, which are always bone-porcelain (dark world) or oxidized-graphite (light world) and change state by opacity alone.
Do hold body measure at ~60ch and keep the cinematic motion behind a prefers-reduced-motion crossfade fallback.
donts: Don't ship a generic Squarespace/template portfolio — a white grid of equal thumbnails with a neutral sans and no point of view.
Don't apply startup/SaaS polish: no bright/rounded/gradient-accent styling, no hero-metric blocks, no product-landing cadence.
Don't drift into gothic/horror kitsch — no skulls, gore, blood-drip, or Halloween darkness. The unease is clinical and refined.
Don't go busy or maximalist: no clutter, no loud stacking, no animation for its own sake competing with the work.

Don't add a structural drop shadow (any hard directional offset simulating a lifted panel) — that's still a bug. Control glow is the only permitted shadow, and only as soft, state-tied emergent light.
Don't use backdrop-blur as decoration or on surfaces — it's allowed only as a ≤3px lift of an interactive control. No frosted panels, no glass cards.

Don't use synthetic-flesh as a static fill, background, or section device (the emergent control glow is a transient, on-attention exception); don't invent a third mid-gray ground; don't set body type above weight 300.
